design:
Decisions (operator, 2026-11-10):
- New folder → repository plus a first commit holding AGENTS.md. Not only `git init`: a repository with no commit cannot give agents worktrees.
- Existing folder without git → never committed unasked. A first commit would include whatever is already there (secrets, large files); the operator is offered it with the list of what it would hold.
- AGENTS.md becomes the project's instructions only where the operator has chosen it: automatically when AgentWeave created the file (a new folder, or "Make this a git repository"), and otherwise only when the operator switches on "Use AGENTS.md as this project's instructions". A project with its own AGENTS.md (this repository has one: a hand-written 2.9 KB pointer to CLAUDE.md) keeps exactly today's behaviour until then. (Narrowed after the operator asked how instructions reach agents today: carrying an existing AGENTS.md into every turn would have added a redundant copy for Claude agents in repositories that already arrange their own instruction files.)
- A created AGENTS.md starts with a short AgentWeave section.
- AGENTS.md is not created when the folder already holds AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md or .github/copilot-instructions.md, or is already an AgentWeave project.
- Saving Instructions to AGENTS.md commits it on the project's main branch, so agents' worktrees pick it up when they next merge main.
- Instructions already in the Hub's database move into AGENTS.md when AGENTS.md becomes the project's instructions, so there is one copy.

Hazard (Tier 2): project creation writes to disk; the Hub commits on the main branch; the instructions' source reaching every turn changes for opted-in projects; and recording whether a project uses AGENTS.md is a stored project setting, so a migration is likely — the operator's :8000 runs this checkout's migrations on its next restart, so the migration follows the repository's migration checklist and is additive with a default that preserves today's behaviour. Rollback: the database instructions row is kept (not read while AGENTS.md is in use), so reverting returns to it unchanged.

Drives (readiness review, 2026-11-10): run on a Hub started from the checkout's source on a temporary database (DATABASE_URL to a temp file, a free port). Never :8000. Not the trial Hub :8010 either: its database holds enabled jobs that would fire. A real agent turn in a drive binds a Haiku runner.

problem: Operator, 2026-11-10: git should be a more default behaviour for AgentWeave, and a new project should start with an AGENTS.md carrying AgentWeave's guidance. Today (code, 2026-11-10) creating a project in a new folder makes an empty folder (hub/hub/project_lifecycle.py create_new) and opening one only registers it, so a new project has no repository, its writing agents cannot get their own worktrees (they need a commit), and the Hub's ignore rules are not written (repo_hygiene.seed_repo_excludes returns when there is no .git). Project instructions are a database row (hub/hub/api/v1/instructions.py) put into the context file the Hub hands each run (hub/hub/api/v1/agents.py:2903; for Claude Code via --append-system-prompt-file, runner_commands.py:270). The Hub reads neither CLAUDE.md nor AGENTS.md; each CLI reads its own file from the folder it runs in (Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md; Codex, Kimi and OpenCode read AGENTS.md).

requirements.rationale: Writing agents get their own worktrees only once a commit exists; a repository with no commit leaves them all sharing one checkout.
requirements.statement: Creating a project in a folder that does not yet exist leaves that folder a git repository with exactly one commit, which holds AGENTS.md and nothing else, and sets the project's main branch to the branch that commit is on.
In a repository AgentWeave creates, the Hub's own working files (.agentweave/) are ignored from the start and never appear in the first commit or as untracked changes.

requirements.rationale: A folder that already instructs its agents belongs to someone who chose that; AgentWeave adding a second file would contradict or duplicate it.
requirements.statement: AgentWeave creates AGENTS.md only when the folder holds none of AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md or .github/copilot-instructions.md and is not already an AgentWeave project; otherwise it writes no instruction file.

A created AGENTS.md begins with a short AgentWeave section saying the project is worked on through AgentWeave and where its specifications live, followed by an empty place for the project's own instructions.
Opening an existing folder that is not a git repository creates no repository, no commit and no file in it.

requirements.rationale: An unasked first commit could publish secrets or bulk files into history; showing them first is what makes the one-click action safe.
requirements.statement: For a project whose folder is not a git repository, the operator can make it one in a single action that first shows every file the first commit would hold (with ignored files left out) and creates the repository and commit only on confirmation; AGENTS.md is added by the same rule as a new folder.

requirements.rationale: Repositories that already arrange their own instruction files keep working as they do; a new project gets one source of instructions from the start.
requirements.statement: AGENTS.md is the project's instructions when AgentWeave created it, or when the operator has switched on 'Use AGENTS.md as this project's instructions' (offered in Settings → Instructions only when the folder holds an AGENTS.md). For any other project, instructions come from the Hub exactly as before and the Hub carries no instruction file.

requirements.rationale: Instructions in the repository are versioned with the code and read by tools outside AgentWeave.
requirements.statement: While AGENTS.md is the project's instructions, Settings → Instructions shows that file's content and saving writes it to the file; the 40,000-character limit still applies.

requirements.rationale: Agents work in their own worktrees and see main's committed state; an uncommitted edit would never reach them, and overwriting the operator's own unsaved edit would lose work.
requirements.statement: Saving Instructions to AGENTS.md commits AGENTS.md, and only AGENTS.md, on the project's main branch. If AGENTS.md has uncommitted changes in the project checkout, or the checkout is not on the main branch, the save is refused saying which, and nothing is overwritten; if the project has no main branch set, the file is written and the operator is told it was not committed.

requirements.rationale: One copy: two sources of instructions drift, and an agent cannot tell which one is meant.
requirements.statement: When AGENTS.md becomes the instructions of a project that holds instructions in the Hub's database, those instructions are added to AGENTS.md's instructions area once, committed as a save is; from then on the file is the only source, and the database copy is kept but not read.

requirements.rationale: Codex, Kimi and OpenCode read AGENTS.md themselves; carrying it twice pays for it twice on every turn.
requirements.statement: Every agent turn carries the project's instructions exactly once, whether or not the agent's runner also reads AGENTS.md on its own.

in_scope: Creating a project in a new folder: repository, first commit, AGENTS.md, the Hub's ignore rules

non_goals: Creating AGENTS.md in a folder that already has any agent instruction file or is already an AgentWeave project
Changing anything for a project with its own AGENTS.md until the operator opts in
Committing anything in an existing folder without the operator's action, other than AGENTS.md when the operator saves Instructions or opts in
Pushing, adding remotes or choosing a hosting service
The set-up list that surfaces the offer — slice a-project-says-what-it-needs; this slice provides the action it links to
Reading or editing CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md or other tools' files

summary: Git becomes AgentWeave's default. A project created in a new folder becomes a repository whose first commit holds an AGENTS.md; an existing folder without git can be made one in a single action after seeing what the first commit would hold. An AGENTS.md that AgentWeave created — or one the operator chooses to adopt — becomes the project's instructions: edited from Settings → Instructions, committed on the main branch when saved, and carried once into every agent turn. A project with its own instruction files keeps today's behaviour until the operator opts in.
